claim: TM287/288 is a heterodimeric ABC exporter from Thermotoga maritima that contains a non-canonical ATP binding site.
source: DEER measurements on the heterodimeric ABC exporter TM287/288 from Thermotoga maritima, which contains a non-canonical ATP binding site, revealed that in the presence of nucleotides the transporter exists in an IF/OF equilibrium.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and is supported by references to the protein's origin and structural features throughout the manuscript.

claim: In the presence of nucleotides, TM287/288 exists in an inward-facing/outward-facing (IF/OF) equilibrium.
source: DEER measurements on the heterodimeric ABC exporter TM287/288 from Thermotoga maritima, which contains a non-canonical ATP binding site, revealed that in the presence of nucleotides the transporter exists in an IF/OF equilibrium.
evidence: This is a primary finding from DEER measurements presented in the manuscript.

claim: ATP binding alone is sufficient to partially populate the OF state in TM287/288.
source: While ATP binding was sufficient to partially populate the OF state, nucleotide trapping in the pre- or post-hydrolytic state was required for a pronounced conformational shift.
evidence: This is directly stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data with ATP-EDTA conditions.

claim: Nucleotide trapping in the pre- or post-hydrolytic state is required for a pronounced conformational shift to the OF state in TM287/288.
source: While ATP binding was sufficient to partially populate the OF state, nucleotide trapping in the pre- or post-hydrolytic state was required for a pronounced conformational shift.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated through experiments with E-to-Q mutant and vanadate trapping.

claim: At physiologically high temperatures and in the absence of nucleotides, the NBDs of TM287/288 disengage asymmetrically while the conformation of the TMDs remains unchanged.
source: At physiologically high temperatures and in the absence of nucleotides, the NBDs disengage asymmetrically while the conformation of the TMDs remains unchanged.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by DEER measurements at 80°C shown in Figure 6.

claim: Nucleotide binding at the degenerate ATP site prevents complete NBD separation in TM287/288.
source: Nucleotide binding at the degenerate ATP site prevents complete NBD separation, a molecular feature differentiating heterodimeric from homodimeric ABC exporters.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by structural analysis and DEER data comparing nucleotide-bound and apo states.

claim: The prevention of complete NBD separation by nucleotide binding at the degenerate site is a molecular feature differentiating heterodimeric from homodimeric ABC exporters.
source: Nucleotide binding at the degenerate ATP site prevents complete NBD separation, a molecular feature differentiating heterodimeric from homodimeric ABC exporters.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by comparative analysis with MsbA and other homodimeric transporters.

claim: TM287/288 exhibits hydrolysis-independent closure of the NBD dimer.
source: Our data suggest hydrolysis-independent closure of the NBD dimer, which is further stabilized as the consensus site nucleotide is committed to hydrolysis.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated by ATP-EDTA experiments showing OF state population without hydrolysis.

claim: NBD dimer closure is further stabilized when the consensus site nucleotide is committed to hydrolysis.
source: Our data suggest hydrolysis-independent closure of the NBD dimer, which is further stabilized as the consensus site nucleotide is committed to hydrolysis.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experiments with vanadate trapping and E-to-Q mutant.

claim: ABC exporters pump substrates across the membrane by coupling ATP-driven movements of nucleotide binding domains (NBDs) to the transmembrane domains (TMDs).
source: ABC exporters pump substrates across the membrane by coupling ATP-driven movements of nucleotide binding domains (NBDs) to the transmembrane domains (TMDs), which switch between inward- and outward-facing (IF, OF) orientations.
evidence: This is a well-established mechanism in the field, stated in the abstract.

claim: TMDs of ABC exporters switch between inward-facing and outward-facing orientations.
source: ABC exporters pump substrates across the membrane by coupling ATP-driven movements of nucleotide binding domains (NBDs) to the transmembrane domains (TMDs), which switch between inward- and outward-facing (IF, OF) orientations.
evidence: This is a fundamental characteristic of ABC exporters stated in the abstract.

claim: More than forty human ABC exporters fulfill vital functions in the body by translocating a wide range of cargoes across lipid bilayers.
source: Transport processes mediated by more than forty human ABC exporters fulfil vital functions in our body as they translocate an extraordinarily wide range of cargoes such as lipids, peptides, ions and drugs across lipid bilayers.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and represents established knowledge about human ABC exporters.

claim: Cystic fibrosis is directly linked to ABC transporter malfunction (CFTR).
source: A number of severe hereditary diseases including cystic fibrosis and insulin secretion disorders such as neonatal diabetes and hyperinsulinism are directly linked to ABC transporter malfunction (CFTR and SUR1, respectively), underpinning their paramount importance in human health (Aittoniemi et al., 2009; Gadsby et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Insulin secretion disorders such as neonatal diabetes and hyperinsulinism are directly linked to ABC transporter malfunction (SUR1).
source: A number of severe hereditary diseases including cystic fibrosis and insulin secretion disorders such as neonatal diabetes and hyperinsulinism are directly linked to ABC transporter malfunction (CFTR and SUR1, respectively), underpinning their paramount importance in human health (Aittoniemi et al., 2009; Gadsby et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: P-glycoprotein, ABCG2 and MRP1 act as multidrug efflux pumps in tumors and hamper effective cancer treatment.
source: The human ABC exporters P-glycoprotein, ABCG2 and MRP1 act as multidrug efflux pumps in tumors and hamper effective cancer treatment (Gottesman et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: ABC exporters minimally consist of two transmembrane domains (TMDs) each containing six transmembrane helices and two nucleotide binding domains (NBDs).
source: ABC exporters minimally consist of two transmembrane domains (TMDs) each containing six transmembrane helices protruding far into the cytoplasm and two nucleotide binding domains (NBDs), which undergo large conformational changes in response to ATP binding and hydrolysis (Seeger and van Veen, 2009).
evidence: This is a structural description of ABC exporters stated in the introduction with citation.

claim: NBDs undergo large conformational changes in response to ATP binding and hydrolysis.
source: ABC exporters minimally consist of two transmembrane domains (TMDs) each containing six transmembrane helices protruding far into the cytoplasm and two nucleotide binding domains (NBDs), which undergo large conformational changes in response to ATP binding and hydrolysis (Seeger and van Veen, 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: NBDs are called 'closed' when they sandwich two ATP molecules at their head-to-tail dimer interface.
source: NBDs are called 'closed' when they sandwich two ATP molecules at their head-to-tail dimer interface or 'open' when they are partially or completely disengaged from each other.
evidence: This is a definition provided in the introduction based on established knowledge.

claim: NBDs are called 'open' when they are partially or completely disengaged from each other.
source: NBDs are called 'closed' when they sandwich two ATP molecules at their head-to-tail dimer interface or 'open' when they are partially or completely disengaged from each other.
evidence: This is a definition provided in the introduction based on established knowledge.

claim: The NBDs are coupled to the TMDs via two main and two accessory coupling helices.
source: The NBDs are coupled to the TMDs via two main and two accessory coupling helices (Dawson and Locher, 2006).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: When the NBDs are disengaged, the TMDs adopt an IF state.
source: When the NBDs are disengaged, the TMDs adopt an IF state (Ward et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: The TMDs adopt an outward-facing or outward-occluded state when the NBDs are closed.
source: In contrast, the TMDs adopt an outward-facing or outward-occluded state when the NBDs are closed (Dawson and Locher, 2006; Choudhury et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: An affinity switch is a prerequisite for uphill transport of substrates in ABC exporters.
source: An affinity switch is a prerequisite for uphill transport of substrates, namely substrates need to bind with higher affinity to the inward-facing transporter than to the outward-facing transporter (Higgins and Linton, 2004; Sauna and Ambudkar, 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Substrates need to bind with higher affinity to the inward-facing transporter than to the outward-facing transporter for uphill transport.
source: An affinity switch is a prerequisite for uphill transport of substrates, namely substrates need to bind with higher affinity to the inward-facing transporter than to the outward-facing transporter (Higgins and Linton, 2004; Sauna and Ambudkar, 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: ABCA4 imports N-retinylidene-phosphatidylethanolamine, representing a deviation from the general substrate pathway.
source: Deviations from this general substrate pathway exist for ABCA4, which in fact imports N-retinylidene-phosphatidylethanolamine (i.e. an inverse affinity switch must exist) (Quazi et al., 2012) and for ABC exporters transporting substrates which are too large to be accommodated in the cavity as it is proposed for PglK transporting lipid-linked oligosaccharides (Perez et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: In the ATP-switch model, ATP binding leads to NBD closure and a concomitant switch from the IF to the OF state.
source: In the prevalent ATP-switch model postulated by Higgins and co-workers, ATP binding leads to NBD closure and a concomitant switch from the IF to the OF state (Higgins and Linton, 2004).
evidence: This is a description of the ATP-switch model stated in the introduction with citation.

claim: In the ATP-switch model, ATP hydrolysis destabilizes the NBD dimer and the transporter reverts to its IF state with disengaged NBDs.
source: ATP hydrolysis then destabilizes the NBD dimer and the transporter reverts to its IF state with disengaged NBDs.
evidence: This is part of the ATP-switch model description in the introduction.

claim: In the ATP-switch model, ATP hydrolysis is not required for substrate release.
source: In the ATP-switch model, ATP hydrolysis is not required for substrate release; the entire transport reaction of a substrate is coupled to ATP binding to the NBD sandwich dimer and the role of ATP hydrolysis is to recharge the machinery for the next ATP binding and substrate transport reaction.
evidence: This is a key feature of the ATP-switch model described in the introduction.

claim: All spin-labeled mutants of TM287/288 retained robust ATPase activity (>90%).
source: All spin-labeled mutants (spin labeling efficiency >70%) were shown to retain robust ATPase activity (>90%) (Table 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Table 1.

claim: All spin-labeled mutants of TM287/288 exhibited robust ATPase stimulation upon addition of Hoechst 33342.
source: All spin-labeled mutants exhibited a robust ATPase stimulation upon addition of Hoechst 33342 which was maximal at 50 µM or 100 µM Hoechst 33342 depending on the mutant investigated.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The six interspin distances measured in the apo state of TM287/288 are in agreement with the crystallized IF conformation.
source: The six interspin distances measured in the apo state of the transporter are in agreement with the crystallized IF conformation (Figure 1 and Figure 1—figure supplement 1) based on the MMM simulations, which were previously shown to provide a 3.5–4 Å root mean square deviation (rmsd) between experimental and calculated mean distances (Jeschke, 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by comparison with crystal structure and MMM simulations.

claim: Addition of ATP-Vi-Mg induced distinct distance changes in all six pairs of TM287/288 compared to the apo state.
source: Addition of ATP-Mg in the presence of vanadate (ATP-Vi-Mg) induced distinct distance changes in all six pairs compared to the apo state (Figure 2, magenta versus cyan lines).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2.

claim: ADP trapping by vanadate switched the great majority of TM287/288 transporters to a conformation strongly resembling the homology model based on the outward-facing structure of Sav1866.
source: ADP trapping by vanadate, which is expected to occur in the catalytically active consensus site, switched the great majority of the transporters to a conformation strongly resembling the homology model based on the outward-facing structure of Sav1866 (Figure 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by DEER data in Figure 2.

claim: A high fraction of OF states in TM287/288 was obtained by incubating with ATP-Mg for 20 s at 25°C.
source: A high fraction of OF states was also obtained by incubating spin-labeled TM287/288 with ATP-Mg for 20 s at 25°C (Figure 2, red lines).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2.

claim: TM287/288 ATP hydrolysis at 25°C is comparatively slow with a turnover rate of 11 ATP min−1.
source: Since TM287/288 stems from the hyperthermophilic bacterium Thermotoga maritima, ATP hydrolysis at 25°C is comparatively slow (turnover rate of 11 ATP min−1, Table 1) and thereby resembles the experimental condition of ATP hydrolysis inhibited by vanadate at 50°C (turnover rate of 22 ATP min−1, Table 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Table 1.

claim: Vanadate has a Ki of 75.1 ± 11.4 nM for TM287/288 at 50°C.
source: Based on fitting and calculations as outlined in the material and methods, vanadate has a Ki of 75.1 ± 11.4 nM (Table 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Table 2 and Figure 3B.

claim: At 1 mM vanadate concentration, the residual ATPase activity of TM287/288 was 8% at 50°C.
source: Of note, at 1 mM vanadate concentration the residual ATPase activity was 8% (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The vanadate-trapped state of TM287/288 is not very stable and a fraction of transporters run through the transport cycle.
source: This indicates that the vanadate-trapped state of TM287/288 is not very stable and a fraction of transporters run through the transport cycle.
evidence: This is an interpretation stated in the Results section based on the residual ATPase activity data.

claim: Addition of AMP-PNP-Mg to TM287/288 resulted only in modest conformational changes.
source: In agreement with our previous study (Hohl et al., 2014), addition of the nucleotide analog AMP-PNP-Mg resulted only in modest conformational changes, most likely originating from the reorientation of the spin-labeled side chains (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by DEER data.

claim: AMP-PNP-Mg binding does not support the conformational switch to the OF state in TM287/288.
source: Thus, AMP-PNP-Mg binding does not support the conformational switch to the OF state in TM287/288, neither in detergent nor in proteoliposomes (Hohl et al., 2014) (Figure 2—figure supplements 2–3).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by DEER data.

claim: When ATPγS-Mg was added to TM287/288, a fraction of transporters adopted the OF state while a detectable fraction stayed in an apo-like conformation.
source: By contrast, when the ATP analog ATPγS-Mg was added, a fraction of transporters was found to adopt the OF state, while a detectable fraction stayed in an apo-like conformation (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: There is a clear difference between AMP-PNP-Mg and ATPγS-Mg in terms of their ability to switch the conformation of TM287/288.
source: Hence, there is a clear difference between the two broadly used ATP analogs AMP-PNP-Mg and ATPγS-Mg in terms of their ability to switch the conformation of TM287/288.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on comparison of DEER data.

claim: Direct incubation with ADP-Mg prevalently populated an IF conformation of TM287/288.
source: Direct incubation with the hydrolysis product ADP-Mg prevalently populated an IF conformation of the transporter (Figure 2—figure supplement 3, orange lines).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: At 50°C, ATPγS has a Ki of 0.0439 ± 0.0062 µM for TM287/288.
source: When the ATPase assay was performed at 50°C, we determined Ki values of 0.0439 ± 0.0062 µM, 0.246 ± 0.042 µM and 10.4 ± 2.9 µM for ATPγS, AMP-PNP and ADP, respectively (Table 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Table 2.

claim: At 50°C, AMP-PNP has a Ki of 0.246 ± 0.042 µM for TM287/288.
source: When the ATPase assay was performed at 50°C, we determined Ki values of 0.0439 ± 0.0062 µM, 0.246 ± 0.042 µM and 10.4 ± 2.9 µM for ATPγS, AMP-PNP and ADP, respectively (Table 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Table 2.

claim: At 50°C, ADP has a Ki of 10.4 ± 2.9 µM for TM287/288.
source: When the ATPase assay was performed at 50°C, we determined Ki values of 0.0439 ± 0.0062 µM, 0.246 ± 0.042 µM and 10.4 ± 2.9 µM for ATPγS, AMP-PNP and ADP, respectively (Table 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Table 2.

claim: At both 25°C and 50°C, ATPγS is the strongest inhibitor of ATP hydrolysis in TM287/288.
source: These measurements revealed that at both temperatures ATPγS is the strongest inhibitor of ATP hydrolysis.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on Ki values determined at both temperatures.

claim: TM287/288 is unable to cleave AMP-PNP.
source: We found that TM287/288 is unable to cleave AMP-PNP within the sensitivity of our assay (<0.01 Pi min−1) (Table 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Table 1.

claim: DEER measurements on TM287/288 samples pre-incubated with ATP-EDTA revealed that a fraction of transporters underwent the conformational transition to the OF state.
source: DEER measurements on samples pre-incubated with ATP-EDTA revealed that a fraction of transporters underwent the conformational transition to the OF state, while the majority stayed in an apo-like IF conformation (Figure 2, green lines).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2.

claim: In TM287/288, the transition to the OF state does not strictly require ATP hydrolysis.
source: Thus, in TM287/288 the transition to the OF state does not strictly require ATP hydrolysis.
evidence: This is a key conclusion stated in the Results section based on ATP-EDTA experiments.

claim: ATP binding alone (even in the complete absence of magnesium) is sufficient to induce the IF to OF transition in TM287/288.
source: Instead, in agreement with the ATP switch model (Higgins and Linton, 2004) solely ATP binding (even in the complete absence of magnesium) is sufficient to induce the transition.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on ATP-EDTA experiments.

claim: The E-to-Q mutant of TM287/288 has an ATPase turnover rate of 0.022 ATP min−1 at 25°C.
source: The ATPase turnover rate of the E-to-Q mutant was 0.022 ATP min−1 at 25°C (Table 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Table 1.

claim: At least 78% of E-to-Q mutant transporters have never undergone a hydrolysis cycle during the 10 min incubation period with ATP-Mg at 25°C.
source: In other words, at least 78% of the transporters have never undergone a hydrolysis cycle during the incubation period.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on calculation from the turnover rate.

claim: Addition of ATP-Mg to the E-to-Q mutant resulted in the almost complete switch of the transporters to the OF state.
source: Addition of ATP-Mg resulted in the almost complete switch of the transporters to the OF state (Figure 4, red lines).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4.

claim: ATP hydrolysis is not necessary for the conformational switch in the E-to-Q mutant of TM287/288.
source: Since the great majority of transporters have not undergone a single ATP hydrolysis reaction prior to sample freezing, we can conclude that ATP hydrolysis is not necessary for the conformational switch in the E-to-Q mutant.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Results section based on the E-to-Q mutant data.

claim: The E-to-Q mutation stalls the ATP hydrolysis reaction in the pre-hydrolytic state.
source: Rather, the E-to-Q mutation stalls the ATP hydrolysis reaction in the pre-hydrolytic state.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the E-to-Q mutant behavior.

claim: Addition of ATP-EDTA to the E-to-Q mutant resulted in an almost complete switch from the IF to the OF state.
source: Notably, addition of ATP-EDTA to the transporter carrying the E-to-Q mutation also resulted in an almost complete switch from the IF to the OF state (Figure 4, green lines).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4.

claim: The E-to-Q mutant of TM287/288 has an altered energy profile, resulting in a higher overall propensity to adopt the OF state.
source: Our data therefore suggest that the E-to-Q mutant has an altered energy profile, resulting in a higher overall propensity to adopt the OF state.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the E-to-Q mutant data.

claim: The rank of nucleotides with respect to increasing fractions of OF populations in TM287/288 is: ADP-Mg ≈ AMP-PNP-Mg < ATP-EDTA < ATPγS-Mg < ATP-Mg < ATP-Vi-Mg.
source: The rank of nucleotides with respect to increasing fractions of the OF populations (Figure 5A) was: ADP-Mg ≈ AMP-PNP-Mg < ATP-EDTA < ATPγS-Mg < ATP-Mg < ATP-Vi-Mg.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5.

claim: The OF state is in general more populated in the E-to-Q mutant compared to wildtype TM287/288.
source: However, the OF state is in general more populated in the E-to-Q mutant, which is best explained by an alteration of the energy profile caused by the mutation.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on comparison of wildtype and E-to-Q mutant data.

claim: Thermotoga maritima optimally grows at a temperature of 80°C.
source: TM287/288 stems from the hyperthermophilic bacterium Thermotoga maritima, which optimally grows at a temperature of 80°C (Huber et al., 1986).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a supporting citation.

claim: Detergent-purified TM287/288 exhibits high ATPase activity at 80°C.
source: Of note, detergent-purified TM287/288 exhibits high ATPase activity at 80°C and therefore is not unfolded or functionally inhibited as a result of heating (Hohl et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a supporting citation.

claim: The biggest temperature-induced changes in the distance distribution of TM287/288 were observed in the absence of nucleotides for the spin label pairs placed at the NBDs.
source: The biggest temperature-induced changes in the distance distribution were observed in the absence of nucleotides for the spin label pairs placed at the NBDs, in particular for the one reporting changes at the degenerate site (pair 350TM287/475TM288).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 6.

claim: Raising the temperature from 25°C to 80°C changed the distance distribution of the degenerate site pair from a monomodal peak centered at 2.5 nm to a broadly distributed pattern featuring distances from 2 to 8 nm.
source: Raising the temperature from 25°C to 80°C changed the distance distribution from a monomodal peak centered at 2.5 nm, which is in line with the apo state crystal structure, to a broadly distributed pattern featuring distances from 2 to 8 nm (Figure 6).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 6.

claim: The temperature effect on NBD separation in TM287/288 was found to be fully reversible.
source: This effect was found to be fully reversible (Figure 7) and posits that the degenerate site is largely destabilized at higher temperatures in the absence of nucleotides.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 7.

claim: The distinct effects observed in the consensus and degenerate sites point to an asymmetric opening of the two nucleotide binding sites at physiological temperature in the absence of nucleotides.
source: The distinct effects observed in the consensus and degenerate sites point to an asymmetric opening of the two nucleotide binding sites at physiological temperature in the absence of nucleotides.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on DEER data at 80°C.

claim: The disengagement of the NBDs resulting from incubation at high temperature is not propagated to the TMDs in TM287/288.
source: DEER measurements on the other intracellular and extracellular pairs indicated that the disengagement of the NBDs resulting from incubation at high temperature is not propagated to the TMDs and does not result in a further opening of the inward-facing cavity.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on DEER data at 80°C.

claim: The NBDs are decoupled in terms of dynamics from the rest of the transporter when no nucleotides are present in TM287/288 at high temperature.
source: In other words, the NBDs are decoupled in terms of dynamics from the rest of the transporter when no nucleotides are present.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on DEER data at 80°C.

claim: The presence of any nucleotide (including AMP-PNP-Mg and ADP-Mg) prevented NBD dissociation at 80°C in TM287/288.
source: Importantly, the presence of any nucleotide (including AMP-PNP-Mg and ADP-Mg) prevented NBD dissociation at 80°C (Figure 6).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 6.

claim: The stabilizing effect of nucleotides on the NBD dimer interface is attributed to the formation of cross-NBD contacts of inward-facing TM287/288.
source: The stabilizing effect of nucleotides on the NBD dimer interface is attributed to the formation of cross-NBD contacts of inward-facing TM287/288.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by structural analysis in Figure 8.

claim: AMP-PNP-Mg presence at the degenerate site leads to a reorientation of several side chains that collectively result in the establishment of a larger number of hydrogen bonds across the NBD dimer.
source: Although AMP-PNP-Mg does not directly bridge the NBD dimer, its presence at the degenerate site leads to a reorientation of several side chains that collectively result in the establishment of a larger number of hydrogen bonds across the NBD dimer, mainly mediated by the asymmetric D-loops of the degenerate and the consensus site (Figure 8).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 8.

claim: BmrCD is a heterodimeric ABC exporter stemming from the mesophilic bacterium Bacillus subtilis.
source: BmrCD is a heterodimeric ABC exporter stemming from the mesophilic bacterium Bacillus subtilis.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: The response of wildtype BmrCD was found to be fully in accord with published data.
source: The response of wildtype BmrCD was found to be fully in accord with the published data (Mishra et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation.

claim: In the apo state, the distances between the two spin labels in BmrCD are broadly distributed, indicative of a large disorder trapped in the frozen molecular ensemble.
source: In the apo state, the distances between the two spin labels are broadly distributed, indicative of a large disorder trapped in the frozen molecular ensemble, which is not further propagated to the TMDs (Figure 9A, cyan line).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 9A.

claim: Upon addition of AMP-PNP-Mg, ATPγS-Mg or ADP-Mg, a fingerprint distance centered at 4.8 nm appeared in BmrCD, indicative of an IF conformation in which the NBDs are in contact.
source: Upon addition of AMP-PNP-Mg, ATPγS-Mg or ADP-Mg a fingerprint distance centered at 4.8 nm appeared in BmrCD, indicative of an IF conformation in which the NBDs are in contact, but not fully closed.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 9A.

claim: The short distance of 3 nm characteristic for the OF state of BmrCD was prominently populated upon addition of ATP-Vi-Mg.
source: The short distance of 3 nm, which is characteristic for the OF state of BmrCD, was prominently populated upon addition of ATP-Vi-Mg, resulting in vanadate trapping at the consensus site (Figure 9A, magenta line).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 9A.

claim: Quick incubation with ATP-Mg induced the conformational switch to the OF state in a measurable fraction of BmrCD transporters.
source: Finally, a quick incubation with ATP-Mg induced the conformational switch to the OF state in a measurable fraction of transporters (Figure 9A, red line), i.e. a condition under which the ATPase cycle is operating, which is in agreement with (Mishra et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 9A.

claim: In BmrCD, ATPγS-Mg could only populate the nucleotide-bound state centered at 4.8 nm, but did not result in the switch to the OF state.
source: In contrast to TM287/288, ATPγS-Mg could only populate the nucleotide-bound state centered at 4.8 nm, but did not result in the switch to the OF state.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 9A.

claim: TM287/288 exhibits a very high apparent affinity of 3.27 ± 0.42 µM for ATP-Mg at 25°C.
source: ATPase activity measurements revealed that TM287/288 exhibits a very high apparent affinity of 3.27 ± 0.42 µM for ATP-Mg at 25°C, whereas the corresponding affinity amounts only to 343 ± 24 µM for BmrCD (Table 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Table 2.

claim: BmrCD has an apparent affinity of 343 ± 24 µM for ATP-Mg at 25°C.
source: ATPase activity measurements revealed that TM287/288 exhibits a very high apparent affinity of 3.27 ± 0.42 µM for ATP-Mg at 25°C, whereas the corresponding affinity amounts only to 343 ± 24 µM for BmrCD (Table 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Table 2.

claim: Addition of ATP-Mg to the E-to-Q mutant of BmrCD induced a complete switch of the molecular ensemble to the OF state.
source: In contrast, addition of ATP-Mg to the E-to-Q mutant induced a complete switch of the molecular ensemble to the OF state, with the 3 nm fingerprint distance between the two labels (Figure 9B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 9B.

claim: The residual activity of BmrCD carrying the E-to-Q mutation was found to be higher than that of TM287/288 E-to-Q mutant.
source: With a turnover rate of 0.09 ATP min−1, the residual activity of BmrCD carrying the E-to-Q mutation was found to be higher than the one of TM287/288.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on comparison of turnover rates.

claim: MsbA partially switched to an OF state upon ATP-EDTA addition.
source: Here, we show that under the same experimental conditions used for TM287/288 and BmrCD, MsbA partially switched to an OF state upon ATP-EDTA addition (as in TM287/288 but in contrast to BmrCD).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 9C.

claim: In MsbA, AMP-PNP-Mg addition supported a complete transition to the OF state.
source: Finally, in contrast to both heterodimeric ABC exporters, AMP-PNP-Mg addition supported a complete transition to the OF state in homodimeric MsbA (Figure 9C), as shown previously (Mittal et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 9C.

claim: In MsbA containing two consensus ATP binding sites, very similar structural responses are induced by AMP-PNP-Mg and ATP-Vi-Mg.
source: Hence, in MsbA containing two consensus ATP binding sites, very similar structural responses are induced by AMP-PNP-Mg and ATP-Vi-Mg (Figure 9C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 9C.

claim: AMP-PNP-Mg is incapable of supporting the closure of the degenerate sites of BmrCD and TM287/288.
source: This finding reinforces our notion that AMP-PNP-Mg is incapable of supporting the closure of the degenerate sites of BmrCD and TM287/288.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on comparison with MsbA.

claim: The findings call a recent study on BmrCD into question, which claimed that ATP hydrolysis is an absolute requirement for triggering the IF to OF transition in heterodimeric ABC exporters.
source: Therefore, our findings call a recent study on BmrCD into question, which claimed that ATP hydrolysis is an absolute requirement for triggering the IF to OF transition in heterodimeric ABC exporters encompassing a degenerate ATP binding site (Mishra et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on the study's findings.

claim: The study highlights the role of a dynamic interplay between coexisting IF and OF states in ABC exporters.
source: Rather, our study highlights the role of a dynamic interplay between coexisting IF and OF states in ABC exporters, which are interconverted in a transporter-specific manner by nucleotide binding and hydrolysis.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a key conclusion.

claim: The interconversion between IF and OF states is specific to the ABC exporter investigated.
source: Rather, our study highlights the role of a dynamic interplay between coexisting IF and OF states in ABC exporters, which are interconverted in a transporter-specific manner by nucleotide binding and hydrolysis.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on comparison of different transporters.

claim: The apo state with the engine decoupled from the rest of the machine is considered an 'off-state' which is rare and not required in the transport cycle.
source: Therefore, we consider the apo state with the engine decoupled from the rest of the machine as an 'off-state' (state 0 in Figure 10), which is rare and not required in the transport cycle.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an interpretation of the findings.

claim: In the crystal structure of TM287/288, AMP-PNP was shown to bind exclusively to the degenerate site.
source: In the crystal structure of TM287/288 AMP-PNP was shown to bind exclusively to the degenerate site.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with reference to crystal structure data.

claim: AMP-PNP does not directly mediate cross-NBD contacts as those found in closed NBDs of TM287/288.
source: Importantly, AMP-PNP does not directly mediate cross-NBD contacts as those found in closed NBDs (Figure 8).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and shown in Figure 8.

claim: Nucleotide binding at the degenerate site of TM287/288 results in the formation of six additional hydrogen bonds and two novel salt bridges between the NBDs.
source: Instead, a comparison of the apo and the AMP-PNP-Mg bound structures of TM287/288 revealed that nucleotide binding at the degenerate site results in the formation of six additional hydrogen bonds and two novel salt bridges between the NBDs via long-range conformational changes mainly involving the two asymmetric D-loops (Figure 8).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and shown in Figure 8.

claim: Nucleotide binding to the degenerate site prevents NBD separation under physiological conditions in TM287/288 and BmrCD.
source: Hence, as rationalized by the comparison of AMP-PNP-Mg bound and apo TM287/288 structures, nucleotide binding to the degenerate site (and possibly also to the consensus site as shown in state 1b), even including the hydrolysis product ADP, prevents NBD separation under physiological conditions in TM287/288 and BmrCD (Figure 10).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on structural and DEER data.

claim: The partial NBD contacts of inward-facing TM287/288 facilitate NBD closure because the NBDs remain appropriately aligned.
source: These contacts facilitate NBD closure, because the NBDs remain appropriately aligned.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an interpretation.

claim: Fully separated NBDs of homodimeric ABC exporters have to sample a much larger conformational space for their correct dimerization.
source: By contrast, fully separated NBDs of homodimeric ABC exporters have to sample a much larger conformational space for their correct dimerization.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a comparison with heterodimeric transporters.

claim: Nucleotide binding to fully or partially separated NBDs of inward-facing ABC exporters is unlikely a requirement for NBD closure.
source: In other words, nucleotide binding to fully or partially separated NBDs of inward-facing ABC exporters is unlikely a requirement for NBD closure.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an interpretation.

claim: The transition between opened and closed NBDs likely occurs spontaneously by Brownian motion even in the absence of nucleotides.
source: Instead, the transition between opened and closed NBDs – and consequently – the transition between the IF and OF state likely occurs spontaneously by Brownian motion even in the absence of nucleotides.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The interconversion between states 1b and 2 is reversible as long as the consensus site nucleotide is not committed to hydrolysis.
source: Our model envisages that the interconversion between states 1b and 2 is reversible as long as the consensus site nucleotide is not committed to hydrolysis.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as part of the proposed model.

claim: Hydrolysis can only occur after NBD closure in ABC exporters.
source: Importantly, hydrolysis can only occur after NBD closure, hence the IF to OF transition must be driven by nucleotide binding rather than hydrolysis.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a key mechanistic conclusion.

claim: The IF to OF transition must be driven by nucleotide binding rather than hydrolysis.
source: Importantly, hydrolysis can only occur after NBD closure, hence the IF to OF transition must be driven by nucleotide binding rather than hydrolysis.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a key mechanistic conclusion.

claim: Once ATP at the consensus site commits to the hydrolysis reaction, the transporter irreversibly progresses first to a pre-hydrolytic and then to a post-hydrolytic state.
source: Once the ATP at the consensus site commits to the hydrolysis reaction, the transporter irreversibly progresses first to a pre-hydrolytic and then to a post-hydrolytic state (states 3 and 4 in Figure 10), which are structurally indistinguishable from state 2 by DEER with the available spin-labeled pairs.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as part of the proposed model.

claim: Entering the hydrolysis reaction strongly increases nucleotide affinity and thereby stabilizes the closed NBD sandwich dimer.
source: The molecular event of entering the hydrolysis reaction – also called nucleotide occlusion in earlier studies on ABCB1 (Sauna and Ambudkar, 2001; Sauna et al., 2006, 2007) – strongly increases nucleotide affinity (highlighted by a red colored ATP in state 3, Figure 10) and thereby stabilizes the closed NBD sandwich dimer.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with supporting citations.

claim: The E-to-Q mutation modulated the energy profile of TM287/288 by shifting the equilibrium towards the OF state.
source: Therefore, our data suggest that the E-to-Q mutation modulated the energy profile of TM287/288 by shifting the equilibrium towards the OF state.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on experimental observations.

claim: AMP-PNP-Mg turned out to be unable to close the degenerate site of TM287/288.
source: Interestingly, AMP-PNP-Mg turned out to be unable to close the degenerate site.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on DEER data.

claim: AMP-PNP-Mg firmly closes the NBDs of homodimeric MsbA by binding to the two consensus sites.
source: This surprising finding explains why AMP-PNP-Mg firmly closes the NBDs of homodimeric MsbA by binding to the two consensus sites but not those of the heterodimeric ABC exporters TM287/288 and BmrCD.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on comparison of different transporters.

claim: ABC exporters have evolved an energy profile that permits them to adopt the functionally relevant conformational states under operating conditions.
source: ABC exporters have therefore evolved an energy profile that permits them to adopt the functionally relevant conformational states under operating conditions.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a general conclusion.

claim: The inability of the catalytically impaired E-to-Q mutant to transport substrates can be explained by an overpopulation of the OF state.
source: The inability of the catalytically impaired E-to-Q mutant to transport substrates can be explained by an overpopulation of the OF state, which prevents the transporter from switching forth and back between its IF and OF states.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an interpretation.

claim: The extracellular gate of TM287/288 is a highly dynamic region of the transporter.
source: This indicates that the extracellular gate of TM287/288 is a highly dynamic region of the transporter.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on DEER data showing broad distance distributions.

claim: Each ABC exporter studied by DEER appears to possess an inbuilt, characteristic energy landscape.
source: Each ABC exporter studied thus far by DEER appears to possess an inbuilt, characteristic energy landscape, which has evolved to pump its dedicated substrates in the presence of high physiological ATP concentrations.
evidence: This is stated in the Conclusions section as a general conclusion.

claim: BmrCD and TM287/288 behave very differently with regard to their conformational dynamics despite both being heterodimeric ABC exporters.
source: Although BmrCD and TM287/288 are both heterodimeric ABC exporters, they behave very differently with regard to their conformational dynamics.
evidence: This is stated in the Conclusions section based on comparison of experimental data.

claim: In BmrCD, the two IF states are clearly preferred over the OF state.
source: In BmrCD, the two IF states (with partial NBD contact or fully separated NBDs) are clearly preferred over the OF state, while from a thermodynamic point of view the two major IF and OF states populated in the presence of nucleotides are closer together in TM287/288.
evidence: This is stated in the Conclusions section based on DEER data.

claim: The results do not support the notion that heterodimeric ABC exporters strictly require ATP hydrolysis to switch to the OF state.
source: Our results therefore do not support the notion that heterodimeric ABC exporters strictly require ATP hydrolysis to switch to the OF state.
evidence: This is stated in the Conclusions section as a key conclusion.

claim: An important functional role of the degenerate site is to prevent full separation of the NBDs as observed in homodimeric ABC exporters.
source: Hence, an important functional role of the degenerate site is to prevent full separation of the NBDs as observed in homodimeric ABC exporters.
evidence: This is stated in the Conclusions section based on structural and DEER data.

claim: The pre-orientation facilitated by the degenerate site may be relevant for substrate binding and regulatory mechanisms in heterodimeric ABC exporters.
source: Consequently, this pre-orientation facilitates NBD closure and may be relevant for substrate binding and regulatory mechanisms in these ABC exporters.
evidence: This is stated in the Conclusions section as speculation.
